tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Stickers and arrows assemble a visual explanation through clearly placed pieces, visible overlaps and short actions.

## Visual identity
Use physical-looking pieces to assemble a readable explanation. Explain a mechanism as a sequence of physical-looking stickers and simple arrows.

## Surfaces and construction
Give stickers clean borders, visible overlaps and consistent shadow depth. Use rounded icons, white cut edges and light contact shadows on a shared surface. Give cut shapes a common edge treatment, a restrained paper thickness and their own contact shadows. Use a continuous border that follows the contour when a sticker bends.

## Colour roles
Use colour to distinguish an active sticker from supporting pieces. Assign stable colours or symbols to repeat concepts. Keep key roles distinct without colour alone.

Example palette. background #F5EFDF, foreground #2C424D, accent 1 #FFFFFF, accent 2 #73A59E, accent 3 #D28C67.

## Lettering and captions
Put approved text on a solid sticker face and leave a clear trim margin. Stagger supporting copy after the main callout so the order is apparent.

## Timing and movement
Let the main sticker peel or land before neighbouring accents enter. Use a short spring about its point of contact and hold the explanation panel after the border settles.

## Framing and viewpoint
Frame a steady explanation surface with all important start and end positions visible. Keep all connected pieces in view when a relationship is first introduced.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, use a light cue on placement or at the end of a cause-and-effect arrow. If enabled, use soft paper contacts and restraint around explanatory speech.

## Characteristic actions
Place two related stickers and trace the arrow that shows what changes between them.

Peel, arrange or connect two pieces, then hold for the relationship to read.

## Review checks
Inspect the most curled and compressed silhouettes. Check that each white border follows its cut shape and that key wording clears the overlaps.

## Implementation tools
Attach border, shadow and anchor to each shape and key their movement together. Use layered vector stickers and keyed strokes, with explicit target anchors for arrows.

## Project choices
Choose a process or relationship that can be built in a few visible placements. Choose a small mechanism, process or explanation with a limited number of concepts per beat.

sources.palette_lesson: The defining constraint is a flat, high-chroma sticker system: black outlines and hard black offset shadows, white card interiors, and a handful of saturated fills that each carry a fixed semantic role (in this example: pink = machine/alive, cyan = channel/receiver, gray diagonal hatching = dead, green check = delivered, yellow = message or highlight, dashed outline = absent). The background works as a flat chapter-coded stage with a subtle same-hue dot grid, and it changes on a hard cut when the narrative question changes. For new subjects, choose a chapter color that suits the topic and keep enough value contrast that white cards and black strokes stand out. Avoid giving an accent its own fill as the background (for example a pink field when pink means the actor). They are not fixed tokens. Note that the canvas tint already changes with the scene in this source, from warm off-white to cool mint, which shows the background is meant to follow the scene. In new projects, keep the paper grain, the matte cut-paper layers and the dark ink type, and choose the paper tint from the subject. Keep strong contrast between the dark type and the light paper, keep accents sparse, and do not let the highlighter or confetti compete with the headline.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> A luminous wireframe and ordered readouts identify one part of a futuristic display at a time.

## Visual identity
Present information as a study of one spatial object rather than filling the view with unrelated controls.

## Surfaces and construction
Build the visible subject as a lit wire cage, filled plane or sparse points with a consistent depth scale. Use restrained fog behind it and draw leader lines in a readable front layer.

## Colour roles
Spend the accent hue on the item just confirmed by a lock or reading. Use one emission family for the wireframe and a separate emphasis value at the selected feature.

Example palette. background #0C1822, foreground #E7F4F3, accent 1 #55C7CF.

## Lettering and captions
Set approved units and labels on stable grid lines. Attach tracking labels to targets with visible leaders and keep persistent text separate from scrolling readouts.

## Timing and movement
Draw the grid or reference geometry first, then acquire a target and update its data after the lock. Hold the labelled result while secondary scanning continues in a small area.

## Framing and viewpoint
Offset the orbit target to make room for readouts. Examine a part with a descending three-quarter orbit, a top view for layout or a held profile for use. Push towards internals, whip with the target indicator, rotate around a part’s axis, or truck along its length. Pull back with a magnifying inset to keep context, crane as the object stands or settles, and complete a turntable when all sides matter. A slow drift can carry reading time. Keep every piece and enabled text inside the frame.

## Sound options
If enabled, use one acquisition sound at lock. Keep ambient electronic layers under key information. If sound is enabled, use small acquisition tones at actual state changes and leave the rest of the display calm.

## Characteristic actions
- Sweep across one shape, lock at a recognisable feature and label it without moving the target.
- Grow the scan, acquire its target, separate the relevant pieces and settle a measured value.

Acquire a visible target, let the marker lock, then draw a leader to the relevant value. If the diagram opens, leave enough of the original frame to identify the parent object.

## Review checks
Inspect the lock frame. A value, label and tracking reticle should refer to the same target while the background passes behind them.

## Implementation tools
Project anchor points from the scene and keep display labels in a separate readable layer. Register the scan, turntable and bracket anchors to the same geometry or projected point set.

## Project choices
Choose an inspection, a verified status change or an explanation of a hidden component. Use an object, environment or diagnostic model. Keep the projected origin and label targets clear.

> Clean frosted panels hold the content while broad, diffuse colour changes give the background slow motion and depth.

## Visual identity
Separate the softness of the colour field from the sharpness of the content. Place sharp frosted content surfaces over slow diffuse aurora colour.

## Surfaces and construction
Use diffuse aurora layers behind a consistent frosted material. Use broad gradient bands, fine panel edges and soft shadows with bounded local blur.

## Colour roles
Give the selected content enough contrast over both light and dark parts of the field. Use a small set of gradient hues and keep background brightness stable behind copy. Assign broad hues to depth regions and keep the brightest areas behind unlabelled panel edges. Choose the reading tint from the darkest and brightest background values reached during the move.

Example palette. background #142535, foreground #F2F6F4, accent 1 #7FAAD0, accent 2 #9B87C3, accent 3 #65AAA5.

## Lettering and captions
Set approved type over an even region of the panel and check contrast over the brightest point of the moving gradient. Use an independent tint if needed.

## Timing and movement
Let the gradient drift behind stationary information. Move the nearest panel on a separate path and hold it while hue changes settle around it.

## Framing and viewpoint
Use a front-readable view with just enough relative motion to show the panel depth. Drift behind the content and preserve readable screen space.

## Sound options
If music is enabled, pace broad colour changes to phrases. Use effects only for visible interface actions. When enabled, reserve an understated cue for the actual content change.

## Characteristic actions
Bring a panel into place while an aurora band passes softly behind it.

Shift colour behind a stationary panel or let a panel move across the field.

## Review checks
Test the frame where the highest value gradient crosses the smallest lettering. Check that background blur changes with depth and panel borders remain visible.

## Implementation tools
Keep gradient, frosted backing and foreground in separate render layers. Render a bounded gradient field behind separate clipped blur and text layers.

## Project choices
Choose a product or information view with room for a quiet moving background. Use panels, a title or a dashboard with a deliberate contrast budget.

Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Liquid Motion without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Contact, flow and viscosity reveal how a liquid moves, mixes, stretches and returns to a surface.

## Visual identity
Let viscosity, contact and surface tension carry the story of the shape. Use viscosity and contact to communicate a liquid shape changing over time.

## Surfaces and construction
Use a continuous surface with stable highlights and a visible support or container. Choose a coherent droplet surface language with plausible highlights and attachment points.

## Colour roles
Preserve contrast between liquid, support and reflections. Use a stable liquid colour or material with distinct edge and interior values.

Example palette. background #171E2B, foreground #F5ECE0, accent 1 #758FC0, accent 2 #C889A6.

## Lettering and captions
Give approved captions a region clear of splash and reflections. If liquid forms approved lettering, hold the complete contour after the last join.

## Timing and movement
Show fluid gathering before the main pour, impact or pull. Time waves and droplets from the contact frame, then hold while the visible surface settles.

## Framing and viewpoint
Use a view that exposes contact and preserves the silhouette through the deformation. Frame the source, flow and receiving surface together for key moments.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, give a droplet contact or split a cue appropriate to the material's scale. If enabled, use appropriate contact, flow and settling sounds.

## Characteristic actions
Form a visible neck between drops and let it thin or join before the final hold.

Show a pour, separation, rejoin or settling action with a readable end state.

## Review checks
Inspect the leading edge, merge and final pool. Check that the flow preserves coherent volume and that highlights follow the actual surface.

## Implementation tools
Compute motion on a deterministic time axis, using authored state or replayable simulation. Use deterministic 2D field shapes or keyed 3D surface deformation. Bake stateful simulation where needed. Represent a small stylised pour with a changing contour and attached droplets, or use a deterministic fluid surface for a complex shot. Keep the surface deformation, foam and highlights on the same clock.

## Project choices
Choose a pour, reaction or transition where material behaviour makes the meaning clear. Use a drop, stream, pooled shape or intentional logo reveal with visible physical cause.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a hovering orb that drops on activation, compresses at contact, and triggers outward surface growth. Select only when that transformation serves the topic and assets support it; do not use this ID for ambient floating or parallax.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

A punctuation droplet can be the persistent focal form as it spreads into the next field; preserve surface continuity. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

supporting_styles.role: Typography: real-font kinetic text that takes over once the liquid gathers into a wordmark or phrase.

suggestions.rationale: Metaballs can't hold accurate lettering, so composited kinetic type gives the formation a crisp, readable payoff.
suggestions.best_for: Brand stings, beverage or cosmetics titles and event openers.
suggestions.video_application: Let droplets gather in #758FC0/#C889A6 on #171E2B, then crossfade to real text in #F5ECE0 at the formation point and hold it still.
suggestions.html_application: WebGL metaball canvas with the heading as DOM text revealed after formation, with an immediate static heading under reduced motion.
consistency_rules: After the handoff the type stays rigid, with no further liquid wobble.
Fluid highlights never obscure letter contours.
Type motion inherits the elastic settle timing.
avoid: Relying on SDF approximations for final legible text.
Long kinetic type sequences diluting the fluid hero.

supporting_styles.role: Timing system: merges, splits and splashes cued to beats from a supplied music track.

suggestions.rationale: Beat-mapped timing gives fluid events a clear rhythm without changing the liquid material language.
suggestions.best_for: Music visualizers and audio-led promos where a licensed track is supplied.
suggestions.video_application: Precompute a beat map from the supplied audio and drive metaball radius and position from it as a deterministic function of time.
suggestions.html_application: Seekable playback tied to audio currentTime, with play/pause controls, captions for lyrics if supplied, and reduced-motion static state.
consistency_rules: Only major beats trigger merges or splits.
Keep the two-accent palette regardless of track energy.
All fluid state derives from the timeline, not live randomness.
avoid: Pulsing on every beat until it reads as jitter.
Using this pairing without a supplied track.

styles.visual_cues: Use concise emphasis text with expressive display lettering, consistent layered outlines, shadows, reaction stickers, and small doodles. Give emotions distinct colors and motion. Time short spring entrances, squash, bounce, and wobble to reactions or verbal stress, followed by readable holds. Three emotion treatments and 9:16 framing are optional examples. Keep faces, dialogue subtitles, and platform overlays unobstructed.
styles.note: A user-requested direction developed into practical prompt guidance. A descriptive broadcast and reaction-text treatment, distinct from continuous dialogue subtitles or general kinetic typography.

tech.implementation: Use actual fonts with SVG strokes or aligned text copies for layered outlines and shadows. Group lettering and stickers into reusable reaction components. Drive scale, squash, and wobble through the selected seekable timeline; preserve reading holds and inspect safe areas against the actual footage.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Expressive type and small supporting marks deliver a quick emotional response while protecting reading time.

## Visual identity
Use an enabled reaction caption to make a visible expression or action easier to read. Give the complete phrase a stable position before increasing the emphasis on one approved word.

## Surfaces and construction
Use bold readable lettering and a limited set of graphical marks. Keep lettering outlines and shadows consistent with the reaction figures and stickers.

## Colour roles
Give the reaction enough contrast against varying background content. Use an emphasis colour for a specific emotion and preserve contrast on all copy.

Example palette. background #FFF5E5, foreground #282E3B, accent 1 #DA855C, accent 2 #668FA3, accent 3 #A47CA3.

## Lettering and captions
Keep approved wording intact and place expressive emphasis on a chosen word. Give the line enough space to survive the strongest pop without moving over the face.

## Timing and movement
Time an enabled reaction word to the readable pose or speech cue, then settle it quickly. Let the rest of the phrase enter at a reading pace and clear at the next reaction.

## Framing and viewpoint
Keep the person or object that caused the reaction visible near the caption. Place the reaction next to, or clear of, the action it describes.

## Sound options
If speech is enabled, use measured stress timing. If effects are enabled, add one cue at the visible impact. If enabled, coordinate the accent with actual visual arrival. If speech is enabled, align a reaction to its actual cue and preserve adjacent reading time. If effects are enabled, cue the settled emphasis or visible reaction without masking other approved audio.

## Characteristic actions
Let a short approved word expand on the key beat and settle with stable outlines.

Land the reaction, add a small emphasis and settle before the next event.

## Review checks
Review the caption once with muted audio. Check the longest line, the fastest entrance and the visible reaction to ensure all three have time to read.

## Implementation tools
Key entry and exit separately from any expressive internal movement. Measure words before keying text transforms. Layer outlined lettering and backing marks independently.

## Project choices
Choose a concise reaction that can be read in one glance. Use a short reaction, verbal emphasis or comic turn that the idea actually calls for.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: Short emphasis captions use layered fill, a heavy dark stroke, a white outer halo and a hard drop shadow. Confetti stars burst on reaction beats. The layout is 9:16, with the mascot kept clear of the text and readable holds after pop-ins.
sources.palette_lesson: These colors are the creator's choices for this short, not a fixed recipe. Each scene uses one saturated, nearly flat background family (golden-yellow stripes, deep indigo, slate blue with a screenshot collage, mint, periwinkle, a yellow/pink/cyan wipe) and changes family at every hard cut to mark a new idea. The parts that stay constant are what define the style: a pastel mascot with a black contour, caption type in white or yellow fill with a near-black stroke, a white outer keyline and a hard offset shadow, plus small multicolor confetti. The heavy dark stroke plus white halo is what keeps captions legible on any field, light or dark. For new subjects, choose the background from the topic and mood. Options include: deep teal or ink navy for tech or night topics, coral or tomato red for urgency, a soft lilac or sky-blue dot grid for calm explainers, charcoal with a neon-lime ring pulse for gaming, warm terracotta or olive for food or lifestyle, or a desaturated photo or screenshot wall as evidence. Keep one dominant field per scene with a quieter same-hue pattern (dots, stripes or rings at low contrast), and reserve the most saturated accent (yellow or hot pink here) for the key word. Recheck contrast between the mascot's pastel fill and the field: pale lilac on mint or butter yellow relies entirely on the black contour.

sources.style_evidence: 9:16 short-form layout with bold white rounded captions, a consistent navy outline and shadow, a pink emphasis word, emoji, reaction stickers (cloud, hearts, sparkles) and an x1→x2 counter. Captions sit in the upper third, clear of the characters.
sources.palette_lesson: The colours here belong to this author's example: a saturated cyan/cobalt sky, golden-yellow sand and turquoise surf for a cheerful beach. The measured dominant colour is just the sand area of the composite, not a style token. What actually defines the style is a set of layer contrasts. (1) A fairly saturated, textured, painted environment carries the setting and mood. (2) Characters use low-saturation pastel fills (peach, cream, blush) inside a single dark navy/ink outline, so they read against any busy backdrop. (3) Captions are white with a dark outline and shadow, which keeps them legible over both light and saturated areas. (4) One warm emotional accent (pink/red hearts, a pink highlight word) is reserved for affection and payoff. (5) Neutral grey props (rain cloud, mailbox) mark sadness or utility. For new subjects, pick the environment from the story and keep the pastel-character, dark-outline and white-outlined-caption roles. Check that the characters' pastel fills still separate from the backdrop (for example, avoid a peach character on peach sand without a contact shadow).

styles.visual_cues: Flat blueprint-blue field; white grid, clean dimension lines, dashed hidden edges and fine hatching. Preserve measured geometry and readable labels.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Fixed 1920x1080 composition with a full-bleed #1B3ED2 rect as the opaque scene field (never cream). Everything is drawn in a single SVG with viewBox in drafting units (1 unit = 1 mm at a fixed scale).

Layers:
- Minor and major white grid lines (stroke-opacity 0.25 / 0.5).
- Object outlines at 2.5px.
- Hidden edges as stroke-dasharray '8 6' at 1.5px.
- Section hatching as a 45° <pattern> of 1px lines, clipped to closed regions.
- Dimension lines with extension lines.

All geometry comes from one measured spec object, so label text is computed from the real dimensions. Labels are HTML/CSS (or SVG text) in a monospaced/technical face, with each label annotated data-reveal-after="dim-N".

Motion: one paused GSAP timeline registered as window.__timelines[id].
1. Grid fades in.
2. Outlines draw with DrawSVGPlugin ('0% 0%' → '0% 100%').
3. Hidden edges draw. Dashing is a mask over a fully drawn dashed path, so it never conflicts with the drawSVG dasharray.
4. The hatch clip rect wipes in.
5. Dimension shafts draw from both ends toward their arrows.

Arrowheads are separate <path data-arrowhead-for="dim-N"> elements, set to autoAlpha 0 and switched on with gsap.set at the exact time the shaft's drawSVG reaches 100%. Each label appears only after its dimension line and both heads are complete.

Preview (3 s): one part view, about 4 dimensions, hatching and labels.
Full video: chains views through labels on the same timeline.

Verify forward, backward and direct seeks at the head-switch times. Use chroma_js to confirm the white-on-blue contrast of 7.88.

Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection:
Measured geometry with readable labels is crisp vector plus real-text territory. SVG keeps dimensions exact and HTML/CSS keeps text measurable. DrawSVGPlugin gives seekable stroke reveals on the HyperFrames GSAP clock.

Alternatives considered:
- Canvas 2D would lose text accessibility and crisp scaling.
- Manim would replace the pipeline.
- Rough.js would destroy precision.
- d3 scales are unnecessary for fixed drafting units.

Tradeoff: dense hatching patterns can alias, so pattern spacing should be checked at 1080p.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> One drafting surface stages aligned technical views, construction marks and dimensions so the object’s structure becomes visible.

## Visual identity
Make the drafting sheet the place where the mechanism is understood. Let a main centre line, outline and annotated operation show how each moving part fits within the same drawing.

## Surfaces and construction
Assign different weights to construction guides, hidden-line dashes, leaders and final outlines. Preserve the paper's grain and keep its darkest shadows outside the detail that has to be read.

## Colour roles
A contrasting mark can identify the single active part while the rest stays within the drawing's ink family. Keep drafting lines bright against one dark blue ground. Reserve another value for construction guides. Use related blue values for the sheet, and assign white or near-white values to the visible technical linework. Give an approved accent a single semantic role such as the part being measured.

Example palette. background #1B3ED2, foreground #FFFFFF.

## Lettering and captions
Set approved notes with a consistent drafting hand and place them in reserved sheet space. Anchor dimensions to the correct endpoints at every zoom.

## Timing and movement
Mark origin and reference axes first. Draw visible outlines before hidden lines and dimensions, then show the mechanism move or separate along those references after the drawing can be read.

## Framing and viewpoint
View the whole sheet to establish scale, then work close enough to read the main drawing. Track along a chain, circuit or force path, punch in on a working part, hold for a decision and turn slightly to reveal thickness. Sweep a section cut through the figure, pan between numbered versions, or move slowly into a major discovery. Use drawing edits and crisp cuts between views. Keep important details inside the usable sheet area.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, use a fine pencil or ruler contact at the beginning of a new operation. If effects are enabled, use different textures for drafting and for the mechanism actually moving.

## Characteristic actions
- Draw the main outline, open an assembly along an indicated axis and close it onto registration marks.
- Build through guides, finished drawing and measurements, then reveal an exploded or sectional view.

## Review checks
Check dash styles, measurement endpoints and title space after an exploded move. Seek directly to a partly drawn state and verify that only the intended lines have arrived. Dimension ticks stay attached to the measured feature. Verify hidden-line conventions, edge alignment and label legibility when the view changes scale.

## Implementation tools
Derive the marks and their dimensions from shared geometry and clamp line weights for close views. Pin measurement anchors to part coordinates and reveal vector strokes by real path length.

## Project choices
Explain a machine, a load path or revisions to one design from the same sheet. Use plans, sections or exploded views. Keep a common origin between them.

styles.visual_cues: Black field with cyan contours, narrow white cores and horizontal scan-line fills. Light is communicated through line density, without blur halos or generic neon particles.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
A Canvas 2D renderer at a devicePixelRatio-fixed backing size. Each frame clears to opaque #07080A. Subjects are authored as Path2D outlines (head/object contours) cached once.

Render per frame from progress values:
1. Scanline fill: clip to the Path2D, then fillRect horizontal 1px lines of #45F0DD every N px, pixel-aligned to integer rows. Line spacing varies with an authored 'light' value per region, so denser lines read as brighter and sparser as darker. Light is communicated only by line density.
2. Contour: stroke the path twice, cyan #45F0DD at 3px, then a white #FFFFFF core at 1px.
3. Optional faint cyan grid behind.

No shadowBlur, no bloom, no particles.

GSAP owns a plain state object, tweened on the paused registered timeline: contour reveal (setLineDash-based length progress from path lengths precomputed via an offscreen SVG getTotalLength), scanline wipe y-extent, and density shifts. A single render(state) is called from the timeline's onUpdate and also after any seek, so direct seeks are exact. Any interior labels use data-reveal-after on their container frame.

Preview (3 s): one subject outline draws, scanlines sweep in top-to-bottom, then density modulates.
Full video: reuses the renderer with more paths.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Luminous outlines and scanning bands reveal the form and texture of a subject inside a controlled light field.

## Visual identity
Use luminous contours and scanning motion to establish an image's form. Build luminous illustration through cyan contours, narrow bright cores and horizontal line density.

## Surfaces and construction
Layer a fine luminous core, wider halo and stable scan lines. Clip scan fills to the shapes and keep the line grid registered through motion. Build a crisp contour, a depth layer and a soft emissive halo separately. Keep the main scan wall light enough to see the volume through neighbouring scan bands.

## Colour roles
Keep strong highlights local and separate them from the backing. Use dark field, cyan bands and near-white cores in their existing roles.

Example palette. background #07080A, foreground #45F0DD, accent 1 #FFFFFF.

## Lettering and captions
Give approved labels a less busy line of the display. Keep text legible when glow and scan bands cross behind it.

## Timing and movement
Sweep a visible scan edge through the object once before drawing in finer lines. Hold the complete volume for inspection and let a loss or repeat of signal affect a specific band.

## Framing and viewpoint
Keep a graphic frontal view and reserve any orbital movement for a legible line object. Show the full form before isolating the scanned area.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, use one brief acquisition cue and leave the scan lines quiet. If enabled, use a scan cue only for the relevant change.

## Characteristic actions
Raise scan density across a contour until a complete illustration appears.

Build a contour with a scan pass or brighten a line at a meaningful contact.

## Review checks
Check object depth during the sweep and review the lowest contrast scan frame on a small display. Keep a direct seek tied to the intended scan phase.

## Implementation tools
Render sharp lines first and grade the glow in a separate pass. Use clipped line fields and deterministic phase with separate core strokes.

## Project choices
Choose a reveal, inspection or image whose shape is readable in light. Use a diagram, silhouette or inspected object whose outline supports the scan.

styles.visual_cues: Sharp silhouettes with a black-to-red-to-orange-to-cream heat ramp, cool narrow extremities and authored hotspots. Distinguish thermal illustration from measured temperature data.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Three.js WebGLRenderer with an orthographic fullscreen quad and a ShaderMaterial, cleared to opaque #080808.

Canvas 2D rasterizes the authored sharp silhouette (head profile) once into a mask CanvasTexture, plus a blurred distance-like copy for interior falloff. The fragment shader computes heat as:
- the interior falloff (core warmer than edges),
- plus authored Gaussian hotspots (uniform arrays: position, radius, intensity),
- minus cooling at narrow extremities (nose, ears) from a thinness term,
- plus slow seeded value-noise shimmer evaluated from uTime.

Heat is mapped through a 4-stop ramp texture (1D DataTexture) precomputed with chroma.scale(['#080808','#C82E20','#F07C30','#FFF1D5']).mode('lab'). The ramp applies only inside the silhouette mask, and edges stay sharp via the hard mask alpha.

GSAP tweens a uniform-state object (hotspot intensities, warm-up progress, uTime) on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate writes the uniforms and calls renderer.render, so seeks are exact.

No temperature scale, degrees or legend is shown: this is illustrative heat, not measured data.

Preview (3 s): the silhouette warms from black through red to cream hotspots.
Full video: alternating paper/red scenes are separate clips; the thermal clip keeps black.

> A sensor-like view maps heat to a stable colour scale so the viewer can see distribution and change.

## Visual identity
Use a recognisable sensor viewpoint and a stable value range to show temperature or a planned illustrative thermal change. Give the viewer visible reference surfaces so heating and camera movement can be distinguished.

## Surfaces and construction
Use the same spatial camera for the thermal and visible views, with material response on each object.

## Colour roles
Keep one temperature mapping and communicate changes of range explicitly. Use one consistent temperature-to-colour scale and reserve contour marks for the shown threshold.

Example palette. background #080808, foreground #FFF1D5, accent 1 #C82E20, accent 2 #F07C30.

## Lettering and captions
Use approved units and a visible scale when values are part of the brief. Keep labels anchored to features and position copy away from the strongest colour transition.

## Timing and movement
Hold a reference thermal view, then let heat appear at its source and spread in an ordered response. Keep the sensor scale stable through a meaningful comparison.

## Framing and viewpoint

Choose a comparison of regions, an inspection of a hidden feature or cooling over time. Show an object, space or process. Label synthetic data clearly and keep measurement units consistent.

tech.implementation:
Opaque porcelain #F0EEE6 field, with graphite #222522 engraved linework in SVG:
- Number wheels: circles with radial tick paths, and digits placed around the rim as SVG text in a tabular face.
- Inspection rails: parallel lines with notch marks.
- Belts: a closed path around two pulleys with tooth marks along a dashed stroke.
- Engraving shading: fine parallel-line <pattern> fills clipped to bevel regions.

Accents: green #416B53 marks the inspection pointer and orange #E78636 marks the active digit. Readouts are HTML/CSS with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

Motion: a single GSAP driver value `drive` (degrees of the input crank) on the paused registered timeline. In onUpdate, every linked part is derived kinematically from it:
- wheel B rotation = -drive * (rA/rB),
- belt tooth stroke-dashoffset = drive * rA * π/180,
- the rail carriage translates by belt travel,
- the wheel digit settles with a detent ease when it crosses a step.

Because no part has its own independent tween, the movement explains a real operation (e.g. a carry: one full units revolution advances the tens wheel one step). Engraved contours first draw in with DrawSVGPlugin.

Any pointer arrows use a separate data-arrowhead-for head, shown only when the shaft completes. Wheel labels use data-reveal-after on their wheel group.

Preview (3 s): a units wheel turns through 9→0 and carries the tens wheel one detent while the belt advances the rail.
Full video: adds operations using the same driver pattern.

> Engraved lines and distinct components show how a real mechanism moves and transfers force.

## Visual identity
Explain how motion and force pass through a real mechanism. Explain a real mechanical operation through engraved components and readable counters. Make the image read as a useful engraved explanation of how the mechanism fits. Use line density for hidden curvature, with the part's external and sectional edges easy to distinguish.

## Surfaces and construction
Use technical contours, engraved hatch directions and legible section faces. Keep porcelain, etched lines, inspection rails, wheels and belts distinct by texture and depth.

## Colour roles
Use value to separate engaged parts and reserve accents for the force path. Use the light field and dark engravings to show component roles with selective contrast at an active mark.

Example palette. background #F0EEE6, foreground #222522, accent 1 #416B53, accent 2 #E78636.

## Lettering and captions
Place approved labels in clear spaces with thin leaders to specific parts. Use enough stroke width to survive at the scale of the engraving.

## Framing and viewpoint
Frame the linked parts and their counters together before showing a close detail. Switch from the complete machine to a close view of the engaged parts.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, place a click on an actual detent or belt engagement. If enabled, use materials and contacts consistent with the actual mechanism.

## Characteristic actions
Advance one engraved wheel and show the corresponding mechanical movement and reading.

Track a gear, linkage or lever through an observable movement.

## Review checks
Check the densest hatch and the narrowest gap. Inspect that any line moving with a part remains registered to the cut piece.

Drive linkage states from shared geometry and derive engravings from stable curves. Bind gear, wheel, belt and counter states to the same mechanical progression.

Choose one mechanism with a clear input, transfer and result. Use an inspection, counting or transmission example grounded in a real mechanism.

tech.implementation:
Three.js fullscreen-quad ShaderMaterial that raymarches an SDF scene: a Mandelbox/Mandelbulb-style fractal solid with a bounded iteration count (e.g. 8 fractal iterations, max 96 march steps, max distance clamp).

Shading:
- normals by central differences,
- one reflection bounce by re-marching along reflect(rd, n) with a reduced step budget,
- soft AO approximated by a few SDF samples,
- exponential distance fog toward #080A0C.

The scene is rendered into a WebGLRenderTarget at about 0.5–0.66 scale and upsampled to the canvas with linear filtering, to bound GPU time per frame. Tone mapping and sRGB output are done once in the final blit.

GSAP tweens uniforms on the paused registered timeline: uEmerge (fog density and fractal power morph), camera position/target along an authored path, and uLandscape (blends the SDF via smooth-min toward a domain-repeated terrain fold). Each update renders synchronously from the uniforms; there is no frame accumulation, so out-of-order seeks match.

Preview (3 s): reflective fractal solids emerge from dark fog with a slow dolly.
Full video: continues into the landscape and later the sunset. Sculptural lettering is planned as an SDF built from a precomputed glyph distance texture, extruded via max(d2D, |z|-h). It is not in the preview, and that limitation is reported.

> A coherent three-dimensional volume reveals recurring fractal forms through shifts in light, distance and reflection.

## Visual identity
Make recurring geometry legible within a coherent evolving volume. Let reflective fractal forms emerge from a coherent volume and resolve into sculptural shapes.

## Surfaces and construction
Maintain stable distance fields, reflectance and depth cues. Build continuous distance fields with stable surface response and controllable depth fog.

## Colour roles
Reserve contrast for the shape or boundary that explains the change. Use a restrained depth palette and keep reflected highlights tied to the scene.

Example palette. background #080A0C, foreground #F2EEE5.

## Lettering and captions
Set approved type in screen space or a quiet view of the distance. Keep lettering outside the high-frequency detail at the front of the frame.

## Timing and movement
Use a smooth advance along a route with measured turns to reveal successive scales. Hold a readable near feature through the change before opening into the next region.

## Framing and viewpoint
Use a slow path that preserves scale cues at the transition between close and distant geometry. Use clean silhouettes and bounded moves to avoid disorienting the viewer.

## Sound options
If music is enabled, pace large form changes across phrases. Keep effects specific to a visible event. If enabled, use cues around spatial changes without forcing a soundtrack.

## Characteristic actions
Evolve a reflective solid into a distant terrain form and reveal one stable sculptural silhouette.

Reveal a new scale through a controlled movement or lighting change.

## Review checks
Review the closest geometry in motion for step artefacts and popping. Check that lighting and scale remain coherent as the route advances.

## Implementation tools
Keep field evaluation, lighting and camera keyed from deterministic time. Use bounded deterministic raymarching with consistent camera coordinates and fixed quality settings. Drive camera orientation and focus along a scheduled 3D path. Limit ray steps by scene scale and use stable sample positions across frames so dense regions do not shimmer during a pass.

## Project choices
Choose one family of forms and a visible traversal between their scales. Select a few coherent fractal perturbations and surface looks, with scope suited to the device.

styles.visual_cues: Powdery chalk marks on black paper with broken textured edges and layered opaque/pale strokes. Preserve a dark paper field; this differs from charcoal drawn on light paper.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #15141A field. A static black-paper tooth texture is generated once into an offscreen canvas from seeded noise2D (low-contrast speckle) and drawn first each frame.

Each chalk stroke is an authored path whose points are sampled at fixed arc-length steps once, cached with tangents. Rendering a stroke up to progress p stamps small irregular dabs of #F1EBDD along the cached samples:
- dab alpha is modulated by noise2D(x, y), which is spatial and seeded, so the same pixel always gets the same grain;
- 'paper tooth' gaps come from destination-out using the cached tooth texture threshold;
- edges break up via a noise-perturbed dab radius.

Layering: pale passes draw at about 0.35 alpha and opaque accent passes at about 0.9, with chalk pressure varied per stroke parameter.

Every frame is rebuilt from scratch: clear, paper, then each stroke up to its timeline progress. Nothing accumulates, so backward and direct seeks are exact.

GSAP tweens per-stroke progress values in order on the paused registered timeline. Arrows drawn in chalk render the head only after the shaft samples reach the endpoint. Text inside chalk-drawn boxes reveals after the box stroke completes.

Preview (3 s): a simple subject is sketched in pale strokes, then opaque highlights are added.
Full video: reuses the stroke library.

Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.

Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.

Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

tech.library_selection:
Powdery broken edges need per-dab raster compositing, which Canvas 2D does deterministically and cheaply. Seeded spatial noise from @remotion/noise (pure functions, browser-safe) keeps the grain stable across seeks.

Alternatives considered:
- p5.js adds a redraw lifecycle for no gain.
- Rough.js produces sketch wobble, not chalk texture.
- SVG feTurbulence filters are slow and harder to control per stroke.

Tradeoff: dab counts must be bounded, roughly 30–60k per frame.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Dry chalk strokes build a drawing in a practical space, with the wipe and residue visible on the dark board.

## Visual identity
Make visible drawing and revision part of the explanation. Use a board and frame that feel like physical objects in a room, and let a wipe, new diagram or corrected mark carry the change.

## Surfaces and construction
Use a wiped slate, wood trim, tray dust and granular pigment that collects at edges. Build dark board stock, visible chalk ridges and low-density dust separately. A wipe should remove the legible centre of the mark and leave a bounded residue only where it helps sell the material.

## Colour roles
Use pale chalk for the base drawing and reserve a distinct colour for the correction. Keep the board dark and even. Save a lighter chalk for the main thought and an accent for corrections.

Example palette. background #15141A, foreground #F1EBDD.

## Lettering and captions
Put approved notes over a clear area of the board and use chalk strokes wide enough to survive at the widest view. Tie callouts to their diagrams with short arrows.

## Timing and movement
Draw the largest strokes in writing order, with a lift at each disconnected mark. Show the wipe clearing the selected region before redrawing it and leave time to read each board state.

## Framing and viewpoint
Keep the camera square to the slate. Track a stroke close, track along a written line or pull to a steady view of the full problem. Revisit an old view to show the answer. Slide a panel in a fixed view; whip briefly along the wall or join views where a stroke crosses a seam. Pull wide enough to establish the tray, frame and surrounding room. Keep reading blocks in frame and avoid extended empty boards.

## Sound options
Use a light grainy drag for enabled writing cues and a separate soft wipe for erasure. When audio is enabled, tie short chalk and wipe noises to contact and keep any narration intelligible.

## Characteristic actions
- Draw the main path in a continuous stroke, erase one claim and replace it in the same position.
- Write a term, wipe only the affected area and replace it while the context remains visible.

## Review checks
Check that the wipe affects the intended ink and dust region. Inspect the lightest lines at the wide framing and make sure a direct seek preserves the board state.

## Implementation tools
Reveal paths in stroke order using board-anchored texture and a separate eraser mask. Make stroke texture persistent per path and reveal erasure with a local mask over earlier marks.

## Project choices
Use one board for a problem, a revision or a sequence with aligned panels. Explain a proof, flow or sketch. Leave some visible chalk residue only where it helps the sequence.

styles.visual_cues: Backlit warm light table with dark granular sand silhouettes, scraped negative-space lines and changing sand density. Light shines through gaps rather than illuminating a white page.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Fullscreen ShaderMaterial on a Three.js orthographic quad.

Canvas 2D rasterizes authored sand shapes (silhouettes) and scrape strokes into two cached mask textures, A and B, for each keyed drawing state.

The fragment shader computes sand density:
- mix(maskA, maskB, uMorph) blurred via a few mip samples, to get soft accumulation;
- minus scraped negative-space lines (an SDF of polylines passed as a texture, multiplied by uScrape progress);
- multiplied by high-frequency seeded hash grain (per-pixel grain fixed in screen space, so it does not swim).

Backlight transmission: color = mix(sandColor #3A291B, lightColor #F5E3B5, exp(-k * density)). Light therefore shines through thin sand and gaps rather than illuminating a white page, with a slight warm vignette of the table (still the #F5E3B5 family).

GSAP tweens uMorph, uScrape and the sand pour radius on the paused registered timeline, and every update re-renders from the uniforms.

Preview (3 s): a sand silhouette thins, a finger-scrape line cuts through, then the shape transitions to the next form.
Full video: chains more mask pairs. This is illustrative granular appearance, not a granular physics simulation.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> The distribution of sand and the light through its gaps turn handfuls of material into a changing picture.

## Visual identity
Show a picture developing from the movement of granular material and light. Make the image from sand coverage and light passing through gaps.

## Surfaces and construction
Separate sand coverage, grain, lit gaps and the hand's visible contact. Keep grain scale visible and register scraped lines to the backlit table.

## Colour roles
Use the light table's clear areas as highlights and thicker sand for value. Use warm transmission for exposed light and dark dense sand for main shapes.

Example palette. background #F5E3B5, foreground #3A291B.

## Lettering and captions
Draw approved large words by exposing the lit surface where this is legible. Give enabled captions a cleared region with compact grain out of the letters.

## Timing and movement
Move sand in a continuous compact push, then sweep or lift fingers to expose the lit table. Allow grains at the edge to settle before slowly revealing a new silhouette.

## Framing and viewpoint
Keep the table plane fixed in frame and crop only for readable granularity. Use a top view for the drawn shape and close views to explain grain handling.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, give a scrape or deposit a short granular cue. If enabled, use grain movement and brief handling cues where contact is visible.

## Characteristic actions
Push sand aside along a contour so the backlight draws a line through the shape.

Gather, sweep or deposit grains and hold the resulting shape.

## Review checks
Check the sharpest transition from dense sand to light in a close view. The grain should move with the sweep and remain stable outside the affected area.

## Implementation tools
Drive coverage masks from keyed strokes and retain grain in table coordinates. Use seeded granular coverage in table coordinates with a deterministic removal mask. Drive grain displacement from the recorded hand path and keep seeded particles stable outside the disturbed region. Let the light show through an explicit sand density mask.

## Project choices
Choose a form or transition that can plausibly be made from a few gestures. Create an original icon, scene or demonstration whose subject can be read in negative space.

tech.implementation:
A perspective Three.js scene with a separately colored environment. The book is two page boards: thin BoxGeometry with visible paper thickness, carrying a #F1E5CE paper CanvasTexture with seeded subtle grain and #342B25 printed linework drawn in Canvas 2D.

Pop-up pieces are thin boxes parented to hinge pivots placed on crease lines, with visible tabs glued to the pages. Each piece angle is derived analytically from the single page-opening angle θ:
- V-fold: piece angles solve the closed-loop hinge constraint, precomputed as a function table of θ;
- parallel fold: the panel stays parallel to the spine.

Creases therefore stay consistent and page mechanics drive the reveal.

The procedural curl technique adds slight bend to large flaps from immutable rest vertices × bend(θ), followed by computeVertexNormals.

Lighting: soft key plus fill, PCFSoftShadowMap contact shadows on the pages, and an explicit ACES tone map with output sRGB checked against the paper tokens.

GSAP owns θ and the camera dolly on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate evaluates all transforms from θ and renders, so seeks are exact. Labels printed on pop-up panels live in the panel textures, so they appear with their container.

Preview (3 s): the book opens from 20° to 180° as one V-fold structure rises with shadows.
Full video: adds pages, each with its own θ track.

Depth, paper thickness and hinge mechanics are defining, so true 3D is required. Flat SVG cutouts would fake it.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Illustrated card folds rise from a visible page. Hinges and shadows make the mechanics of each pop-up readable.

## Visual identity
Keep the book and its miniature story connected through page turns, hinges and tabs. Show what the flat page becomes in the open position before using a close view inside the set.

## Surfaces and construction
Give each card piece plausible stiffness, edge thickness and a distinct hinge. Use printed patterns on the faces and preserve the shadow gap where a card rises off the page.

## Colour roles
Use a controlled local colour family for each spread and keep front and rear card layers legible. Distinguish card faces and folds through paper tone and soft contact shadows.

Example palette. background #F1E5CE, foreground #342B25.

## Lettering and captions
Fit approved type onto a face that becomes flat in the open pose. Keep captions outside the path of the moving pop-up edges.

## Timing and movement
Let a page start opening before the linked folds rise. Show the hinges until they meet and fully hold the raised stage before turning to another page.

## Framing and viewpoint
Treat the book as a miniature stage. Track at eye level with shallow focus, pull to a three-quarter spread, descend from room scale or move in on a character’s expression. Reverse to show the surrounding room, rack between paper and a real object, look straight down at a diagram, hold on a moving tab or crane away. Keep pop-up pieces out of the camera path. Use paper turns, closing covers or a physically motivated cut to change views.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, use a small paper slide and a quiet fold at their own contacts. If effects are enabled, separate page rustle, hinge creak and the contact of a closed cover.

## Characteristic actions
- Pull a visible tab, raise a folded panel and hold as it rests against a clear stop.
- Raise folded pieces in a readable order, turn a page or pull a tab to change the stage.

Raise the scene from rear hinges towards the front as the page opens. Use a foreground flap or tab to uncover a related part once the smaller stage has reached its open position.

## Review checks
Check page pivots and tabs throughout the motion. Inspect the nearly closed state for clipping or a fold that reverses direction unexpectedly.

## Implementation tools
Key parent pages and linkage pivots together and update occlusion as the spread opens. Parent folded planes to hinge axes, constrain the pull path and update shadows from the posed geometry.

## Project choices
Choose a contrasting pair of spreads, a cause-and-effect tab or a scene that travels from room scale into the page. Use one scene, book spread or small card mechanism. Each raised piece needs a readable means of motion.

styles.visual_cues: Overlapping translucent fibers, torn edges and colored tissue layers create underwater depth. Preserve light transmission and overlap rather than opaque cardstock shapes.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #172D3A underwater field.

Each tissue piece is an authored polygon (fish, kelp, light shafts) whose torn edge is generated once: the outline is subdivided and perturbed by seeded noise2D, then cached as Path2D. A fiber texture per piece is generated once offscreen: seeded noise speckle plus short random-but-seeded fiber strokes, with stored seeds.

Per frame, pieces are composited back-to-front with globalAlpha around 0.45–0.6 and source-over, so overlaps visibly compound color and light transmission reads through the stack. The fiber texture is overlaid via 'multiply' clipped to the piece, and a slightly lighter, thinner torn rim stroke shows the paper edge. Tissue hue tokens are additional approved colors only if supplied; otherwise they are derived as foreground #F2EEE1 tints, checked with chroma_js. No arbitrary hues are invented.

GSAP tweens per-piece transforms on the paused registered timeline: gentle sway, a drift parallax with depth-scaled offsets, and layer laydown. Every frame is redrawn from scratch.

Preview (3 s): layers settle into an underwater scene with slow overlapping drift.
Full video: extends the layer manifest.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Torn translucent tissue builds darker overlaps and layered depth without losing the texture of the paper.

## Visual identity
Let overlapping tissue and tone changes explain depth. Show depth through overlapping translucent tissue layers with torn edges.

## Surfaces and construction
Use translucent fibre textures and deliberately torn local edges. Use fibres, distinct layer boundaries and controlled transmission where sheets overlap.

## Colour roles
Show material overlaps through believable mixing and preserve clean paper light. Choose layered tissue colours whose overlap produces believable combined values. Choose overlapping sheets whose transmitted colours remain recognisable individually. Model their intersection from the same transparent layers and reserve darker opaque marks for the strongest silhouette.

Example palette. background #172D3A, foreground #F2EEE1.

## Lettering and captions
Place approved lettering on the least layered paper or on a separate mask. Keep the strongest translucent overlaps outside fine text.

## Timing and movement
Float the first paper shape into place and hold while the overlapping colour becomes clear. Lay the next sheet on a distinct depth so its edge and colour change arrive together.

## Framing and viewpoint
Use shallow parallax with enough overlap in view to show transmission and depth. Use shallow travel that reveals thickness and keeps layers aligned.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, use soft paper rustle on a visible sheet move. If enabled, use a delicate paper contact cue at visible handling moments.

## Characteristic actions
Move a tissue layer past another and reveal the new overlap colour.

Lay a tissue piece, rotate it across another or lift a layer to reveal what is beneath.

## Review checks
Compare overlap colours with individual sheets under the same light. Inspect fibres and shadows through motion so they stay attached to each sheet.

## Implementation tools
Keep alpha and material texture in piece coordinates and composite in depth order. Composite tinted alpha layers with persistent fibres, bounded scattering and independently keyed depth shifts.

## Project choices
Choose a shape progression, a small landscape or overlapping forms whose depth reads through colour. Use underwater forms, atmosphere or an original layered scene that benefits from transmitted light.

tech.implementation:
Three.js scene on an opaque #100D09 background. The vessel is LatheGeometry from an authored amphora/krater profile curve (about 64 radial segments), so the profile stays coherent.

Canvas 2D paints a wide, seamless wrap texture:
- terracotta #BA642F ground,
- ornamental registers (meander and tongue bands) as repeated authored paths,
- a continuous narrative frieze of dark painted figure silhouettes with #F3DFC0 incised detail lines.

The texture's U axis wraps exactly once around the vessel, so the narrative is continuous. No specific historical technique is claimed.

Material: MeshStandardMaterial with moderate roughness and a subtle roughness/normal variation for a burnished surface. Soft key and rim lighting. Tone mapping is checked so terracotta stays in its family.

GSAP owns the vessel rotation and a slow camera orbit on the paused registered timeline. A narrative 'reveal' is a texture-space mask uniform that progressively paints figures in register order.

Preview (3 s): the vessel rotates about 90° as the frieze figures resolve.
Full video: continues the rotation through the whole narrative, with optional close-ups.

> Figures and ornament follow the curved surface of a terracotta vessel, revealing new parts as it turns.

## Visual identity
Use the curved vessel as the continuous surface of the painted story. Tell a continuous painted narrative around a terracotta vessel.

## Surfaces and construction
Choose a supported ceramic reference. Keep ornament, slip and terracotta coherent. Preserve curved pottery, dark silhouettes and ornamental registers that follow the vessel.

## Colour roles
Let painted marks and exposed clay carry the main value contrast. Use terracotta and dark figure pigment with reference-grounded accents.

Example palette. background #100D09, foreground #F3DFC0, vessel material #BA642F.

## Lettering and captions
Fit approved inscriptions inside an open band. Keep captions in a level region if the curved display deforms letters on the vessel.

## Timing and movement
Let action move along a horizontal band of figures. Change poses or let characters pass behind a frame edge at a rhythm that reads around the drawn vessel.

## Framing and viewpoint
Use a view that preserves the vessel profile and paint curvature while the narrative passes. Rotate slowly enough for the sequence and the physical curvature to read.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, add a small turntable or ceramic touch sound at a visible movement. If enabled, keep handling or room cues tied to the real object.

## Characteristic actions
Carry a painted figure over the curved shoulder into the next continuous narrative group.

Turn to reveal another part of the same painted event.

## Review checks
Inspect the turn from front to side. Check that figures and line widths remain readable, and that repeated band patterns meet cleanly at their seam.

## Implementation tools
Map paint to the vessel surface and key turn and light separately. Map the painted scene around a continuous UV surface and key vessel rotation at timeline time. Lay out figures and borders in flat vessel coordinates and project them onto the curved surface. Keep bands aligned when the vessel rotates, including at the texture seam.

## Project choices
Choose an episode that connects around the vessel and fits the historical material. Choose an original narrative motif appropriate to the selected pottery reference.

tech.implementation:
Three.js stone interior: box room with MeshStandardMaterial, cool dim gray stone, high roughness and procedural Canvas grain on a #101216 dark field.

Canvas 2D paints the stained-glass image once: jewel-colored panes separated by dark leading lines. The same CanvasTexture is used twice:
- as the emissive map of the window plane, and
- as SpotLight.map behind the window, projecting that image onto the floor and walls with castShadow.

The window frame and mullions occlude the light coherently via the shadow map. This is a projected-texture approximation, not physically accurate refraction or caustics, and is stated as such.

Post: EffectComposer with RenderPass, then UnrealBloomPass (strength 0 until the finale), then OutputPass for tone mapping and sRGB.

GSAP timeline on the paused registered clock:
1. Dim stone.
2. Blackout: light intensity to 0.
3. Light up: spotlight intensity and angle sweep, and the projected pattern moves across the floor.
4. Final white bloom: bloom strength and light intensity ramp up.

All values are pure functions of time.

Preview (3 s): dim → blackout → colored projection.
Full video: adds the white bloom finale and camera moves.

tech.library_selection:
Coherent occlusion of colored transmitted light in an architectural space needs a 3D light with a projected texture and shadows. Using one shared texture keeps the window and its projection identical.

- Cycles caustics are unavailable.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Lead lines join individual panes whose colour becomes visible in the glass and in light cast onto nearby surfaces.

## Visual identity
Let light reveal a picture in coloured panes and its corresponding shape on a nearby wall or floor. Keep some glass and projection visible together when the relation needs explanation.

## Surfaces and construction
Divide cut glass with dark leads and treat each pane as a coloured filter. Put painted details directly on the glass and keep transmission separate from reflections along the edge.

## Colour roles
Separate the glass's base hue from its transmitted light and avoid bleaching the colours. Give pane groups distinct transmitted hues and keep lead seams dark and stable.

Example palette. background #101216, foreground #F4EEE3, glass ruby #A82E43, glass sapphire #284A9D, glass gold #D6AD52.

## Lettering and captions
Keep approved copy away from narrow bright projections. Use a quiet translucent field or a solid border area whose contrast holds as the light travels.

## Timing and movement
Shift the light to move the projected pattern across a wall or floor. Keep the pane structure visible for one beat before the projection becomes the focus. Give a stepped lead line or crack a clear point of origin and hold its final shape before showing the changed projection.

## Framing and viewpoint
Track beside a moving light band, hold on one pane and pull back to connect it to the window. Track rays to their projection on the floor, hold through a crack and move in on a distant light. Tilt up to tracery, rack between lit and shaded panes, skim the opening at a low angle and return under changed illumination. Use shadows and light passing through glass to connect views.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, keep an understated space tone. Match action cues to any physical moving parts. With effects on, use glass, metal or the surrounding room only where audible action calls for them.

## Characteristic actions
- Travel a soft light patch across adjacent panes and let its floor projection move correspondingly.
- Light a pane in stages, follow a crack or reveal the image again as a projection.

Let light pass through a newly revealed pane and show the corresponding projection move across a real surface. Keep enough of the lead pattern visible to connect cause and result.

## Review checks
Compare the pane colours, occlusion and projected pattern while the light moves. Check the leads on the glass and ensure the projection keeps clean borders.

## Implementation tools
Keep pane IDs and transmission separate and derive their projected position from the light direction. Use separate pane geometry and light projection textures aligned to the receiving surface.

## Project choices
Choose a quiet window, a repair, or a path of light travelling across a room. Use windows, architectural trims or freestanding panes. Preserve glass boundaries and light direction.

tech.implementation: Stage #101820. styles.executable_prompt_template:
> Aligned parts, section views and colour-coded functions explain the construction and operation of a device.

## Visual identity
Let the actual transmission of movement explain the device. Show the order of assembly and what becomes visible between real parts.

## Surfaces and construction
Use engineered component geometry, surface-coloured edges and distinct section faces. Keep fasteners, boards, mounts and surfaces at compatible scale and preserve their source geometry.

## Colour roles
Give power, transmission and sensing visibly different roles in the approved palette. Use an accent to direct attention to the active subsystem. Colour parts by function or material and keep the active joint easy to isolate. Separate materials by finish or value. Emphasise the subassembly without recolouring controlled part codes.

Example palette. background #101820, foreground #EFF4F7, steel #8196A5, glass cyan #61D4DC, flow blue #628BF4, flow warm #EF9F5C.

## Lettering and captions
Put approved part names beside their exposed items and keep callout lines attached as the view moves. Show systems or labels only after the related parts are visible.

## Timing and movement
Establish the assembled item and its orientation. Separate parts along their actual assembly axes in an order that exposes hidden contact surfaces, then pause for labels before putting parts back together.

## Framing and viewpoint
Reveal scale with a rapid withdrawal from detail, then orbit to explain volume or descend through a section. Skim along a force path, hold an overhead for comparison, show an exploded stack from the side and ease in on the contact that matters. Pull back to the whole while keeping the relevant section open. Leave a clear strip for approved labels. Use part movement or the section boundary as a transition.

Orbit while layers separate, skim the finish at macro scale or move into the space between assemblies. Push slowly towards the key part, rise between subsystems and return rapidly or drift above for an overall view. Key the route in the object’s coordinates and ease without passing the intended stop. Offset the view to place labels clear of the object. Keep transitions within the disassembly.

## Sound options
If effects are enabled, place sound at visible contacts. Keep gear or motor loops under the main cues. If effects are enabled, place low-level release and seat cues at the actual connectors. If effects are enabled, tie each contact and powered motion to the mechanism. If audible, distinguish a fastener release from a broad material contact.

## Characteristic actions
- Trace an input through one joint and show the neighbouring component respond under the same timing.
- Open components along one axis, trace a single subassembly and close onto matching alignment points.
- Open a section, separate components along a valid axis or follow the force through a contact. Lift layers in a wave, enter a newly opened gap or close the assembly in reverse order.

## Review checks
Scrub the close approach and widest spread. Check part order, axis alignment, believable internal geometry and whether each label still points to the correct component. styles.visual_cues: Render emissive three-dimensional flame and translucent smoke as coherent volumes with readable depth, buoyant motion, cooling soot and light spill. Maintain a stable dark or contrasting stage, bounded exposure and consistent camera scale. Do not substitute a flat glow sprite, liquid blob or unrelated particle shower for the volume.
